analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. The patch adds a paragraph at head lines 1030-1048 describing a new PromptTokenCache in LocalTokenizerBridge, ChatTemplateLoopRewrites, and the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE=0 kill switch. The supplied units are base text at lines 1210-2007, which sit outside the changed range, so they show only surrounding unchanged documentation. The source implementation (PromptTokenCache.swift, ChatTemplateLoopRewrites) is not supplied, so I could not verify the claims it makes.

Security-relevant claims in the doc text: the token-ID reuse never crosses a cache scope. The scope is presumably the coordinator-authored cacheSalt, as in T-041. The doc also claims token IDs are equal to the unchanged applyChatTemplate path. Sampled background comparisons disable reuse on a mismatch. New long prompts are encoded in parallel on up to four cores.

A documentation-only change cannot regress controls by itself. Questions for the code pass, which this PR's docs do not answer:
1. Whether PromptTokenCache holds plaintext-derived token IDs in process RAM, and for how long. This relates to A-001, T-011 and T-014, and the retention should be bounded.
2. Whether the cache is keyed on the authenticated per-account scope, so no cross-tenant token-reuse timing oracle arises beyond the SEC-035 accepted risk in T-041. A prompt-cache hit would add a new timing channel before the TTFT measurement.
3. Whether the cache is ever persisted to disk. The doc implies it is in-memory only.
4. Bounds on cache memory, which bear on availability (T-029).
5. Whether the rewritten loop templates preserve semantics, since the template affects prompt integrity.

The threat model may need an entry for the in-process prompt-token cache if it is implemented as described. No finding is raised, because the evidence is documentation only and the implementation is outside the supplied scope.
